g.text: Ordinary court-apron air overlap before a bespoke high-force seal
UNADOPTED central air-flow comparison. Actual ends, face tolerances, support and water paths remain open.
Gap exaggerated; actual face control unproved
Nominal overlap 28 − movement 2 − two edge tolerances 1 = minimum 24 mm, authored challenge only.
1780 mm uniform connected gap / 50 Pa / viscosity 1.81×10⁻⁵ Pa·s; Q = b h³ Δp / (12 μ L).
This is an ideal straight-channel sensitivity, not measured leakage or an allocated joint allowance.
No end bypass, workmanship, deformation or loss of overlap is granted a free allowance. Larger gaps challenge the model.
No water head is assigned to this dry apron; quiet −35 / crest +15 do not establish first-leak or capillary performance.
Both floor routes owe the same complete opening. Air leakage alone does not justify a vacuum-style metal seal.
Actual supported overlap / replaceable compression interface, ends, movement and renewal must earn their result.
